title: ggml-cuda: fix divergent barrier in f16 flash attention
body:
## Overview

The issue #27678 reported a divergent block-wide barrier in the `flash_attn_ext_f16_process_tile` kernel revolving around a block-wide `__syncthreads()` in the metadata-combine process.

I moved the block-wide synchronization out of the `threadIdx.y % np == 0` branch so all threads in the `np > 1` case reach the same `__syncthreads()`, while keeping the metadata calculation and SHMEM writeback limited to the intended warps.

## Additional information

The reporter shared that `compute-sanitizer` reveals this issue:

```
compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck --show-backtrace device \
    build/bin/test-backend-ops -b CUDA0 -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT \
    -p 'hsk=192,hsv=128,nh=4,nr23=.8,1.,kv=512,nb=3,mask=1,sinks=0,max_bias=0.000000,logit_softcap=0.000000,prec=f32,type_K=f16,type_V=f16'
```

which reports thousands of divergent-barrier errors.

The issue was initially reported on RTX 4070, CUDA toolkit 13.3.73, driver 610.57.04. I was able to reproduce, fix, and test the fix on RTX 5090, CUDA 13.3, driver 610.43.02.

`compute-sanitizer` reports 3232 errors before and 0 after this fix.

Also, measured performance before and after this commit by running this config:

- **Model:** Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
- **FlashAttention:** Enabled
- **Context depth:** 100k

and the results are:

| Test                         | Before          | After           | Change |
|------------------------------|-----------------|-----------------|--------|
| pp512 @ d100000 (t/s)        | 1390.27 ± 21.66 | 1388.10 ± 21.43 | -0.15% |
| tg128 @ d100000 (t/s)        | 59.75 ± 0.06    | 59.73 ± 0.05    | -0.03% |
| pp1024+tg256 @ d100000 (t/s) | 255.36 ± 0.21   | 255.30 ± 0.19   | -0.02%   |

Therefore, **No measurable performance regression.**
